chunks: Ibn Abi al-Bilād narrated from the one who informed him, from one of the scholars, who said:

The poor believers will be stopped on the Day of Judgment, and the Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He, will say to them: 'Indeed, I did not make you poor due to your insignificance in My eyes; rather, I made you poor to test you. Go forth, and let there be no one who did good to you in the world but that you take his hand and make him enter Paradise [with you].'

key_terms.صَنَعَ إِلَيْكُمْ مَعْرُوفًا: did good to you / did a favor

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the poor believers' role in entering Paradise on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, God reassures the poor believers that their destitution was a deliberate divine trial (*ibtila*) to elevate their status, not a reflection of their worthlessness. He commands them to personally escort every individual who showed them kindness in the world into Paradise, highlighting the profound reciprocal nature of gratitude and social bonds in Shia eschatology. This narrative underscores the virtue of *shukr* (gratitude) and the communal responsibility of the faithful in the afterlife.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.Ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from the one who informed him, from one of the learned scholars who said, “

The poor believers will be stopped on the Day of Judgment and will be told by the Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He, ‘Indeed I did not make you poor due to your insignificance in My eyes; rather, I made you poor to test you. Go forth, and let there be no one who did good to you in the world but that you take his hand and make him enter Paradise [with you].’”
